stories.summary: Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 is finally here, and to play the game natively, you need a PlayStation 5 or Xbox Series X|S. Unsurprisingly, new data shows that PlayStation and Xbox console sales surged in the week before release. According to Circana's Mat Piscatella , there was a "significant surge" in hardware sales in the US for the week that ended November 14. PS5 sales were >2.4x the same...

sources.name: Eurogamer
sources.title: GTA 6 reinvigorates PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series S/X console sales in the US, even at their inflated prices
sources.text: Despite the far higher prices of PlayStation and Xbox consoles today compared to their launch, or even the same period last year, both brands of console saw a significant boost in US sales leading up to the launch of this generation's biggest game: Grand Theft Auto 6. In the week ending 14th November, PS5 hardware unit sales registered a 2.4x increase over the same week last year. Xbox wasn't far behind, seeing a 2.3x increase in its own unit sales. That's according to industry analyst Mat Piscatella at Circana , who pulled the data from Circana's retail tracking service, which covers the US retail market. The PS5 Pro only accounted for less than 10 percent of the PlayStation's total unit sales, by the way, which Piscatella noted was "a LOT better than it has been in recent weeks", and seemingly the result of increased supply. GTA 6, of course, released on 19th November, so the surge in console hardware sales was clearly driven by the rush to attain consoles before the game came out. And while the GTA 6-driven demand isn't surprising, it's worth noting how much more expensive PS5 and Xbox Series X/S consoles are today. A standard PS5 today costs $650, compared to $550 a year ago. The PS5 Pro saw a big jump from $750 last November to $900 today. The base Xbox Series X jumped from $650 last year to $800 today, while Series S now costs $500, up from $400. Even Switch 2, where GTA 6 is not available, saw a notable boost of 40 percent in hardware sales over the same period, driven by The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake and the special edition Zelda Switch 2 console . Circana's November US video game market report, which releases in December, is already one of the most anticipated this year, for digesting and documenting the GTA 6 effect. Worldwide, GTA 6 sold more than 32.5m copies in one day , making Rockstar's parent company Take-Two $3.79bn (£2.89bn) in revenue. We haven't had any updated official sales figures since; but estimates suggest the sales figure could be well into the 40-millions. Perhaps Rockstar is waiting to hit the nice round 50m sales mark before announcing it. If you're playing GTA 6, you may want to keep Eurogamer's GTA 6 walkthrough to hand. It has plenty of very helpful guides covering the game's main missions, as well as explainers for mechanics like romance and the criminal profile , and even cheats for when you finish the game.

sources.title: Retail Hell coming to PS5, Xbox Series, and Switch
sources.text: Publisher Feardemic and developer LEAP Game Studios will release simulation horror game Retail Hell for PlayStation 5 , Xbox Series , and Switch , the companies announced. A release date was not announced. Retail Hell first launched for PC via Steam on May 21. Here is an overview of the game, via its Steam page : Welcome to Retail Hell , the most “beloved” convenience store in Purgatory, where nothing stays stocked, no customer is human, and every shift lasts forever. You play as an overworked clerk stuck in a literal dead-end job. Each shift forces you to juggle supernatural customer service, collapsing inventory, and the unsettling mystery of how you ended up here. In Retail Hell , customer service is eternal. Good luck, management does not believe in refunds.

Caia nas pistas novas ou detone pelos cenários clássicos de Tony Hawk’s Pro Skater 3 e Tony Hawk’s Pro Skater 4, recriados em 4K**, com objetivos mais diretos e o clássico formato de 2 minutos. Crie seu personagem, explore Conton City e treine com mestres icônicos da série para enfrentar inimigos poderosos e proteger o fluxo da História. Sozinho em um bunker abandonado da Primeira Guerra Mundial, com apenas uma bala no tambor, você precisa encarar os horrores que espreitam no escuro. Descubra várias maneiras de sobreviver lá dentro. Na pele do soldado francês Henri Clément, você conta com um revólver, uma lanterna de dínamo barulhenta e poucos suprimentos para coletar e criar itens pelo caminho. Com elementos aleatórios e comportamento imprevisível, nenhuma partida é igual à outra. Caçado por uma ameaça constante que reage a cada passo e som, você precisa adaptar seu estilo de jogo para sobreviver a esse inferno. Cada decisão muda a forma como o jogo reage. Toda ação tem consequência. Além da campanha, o título oferece modalidades multijogador online e batalhas cooperativas contra inimigos gigantes. Com recursos limitados, o jogador precisa administrar seus equipamentos, explorar o ambiente e adaptar suas estratégias para sobreviver a uma criatura que reage aos sons e movimentos realizados durante a partida. Os assinantes do PlayStation Plus têm até segunda-feira (30) para adicionar os jogos mensais de novembro à biblioteca. sources.title: How to Play Grand Theft Auto VI in the Cloud and with Remote Play
sources.text: Grand Theft Auto VI supports XBOX Cloud Gaming , making it available to play even without a current-gen console. With XBOX Cloud Gaming, you can play by streaming it straight from the cloud to your XBOX One, or XBOX Series X|S if you’d like to save some hard drive space. Select Game Pass plans include a monthly allotment of up to 15 play hours, and you can buy more cloud playtime if you need it, giving you the opportunity to experience one of the biggest games of the year on the consoles you already own. The game uses XBOX Series S graphics settings when cloud-streamed with XBOX Cloud Gaming. You can also access Remote Play to enjoy Grand Theft Auto VI wherever you want to play , allowing you to stream gameplay directly from your XBOX Series X|S console to devices you already own, like your mobile phone, laptops, PCs, or even a handheld gaming PC like the XBOX ROG Ally. Here’s how to get these features up and running (a copy of Grand Theft Auto VI from the XBOX Store is required): To start your Cloud gaming session in Grand Theft Auto VI , you can use the controllers that are connected to your console following these steps: When possible, connecting a wired Ethernet cable is the best option for gaming quality. FYI, even wireless networks with high bandwidth can occasionally have a dip in audio and video quality. Remote Play allows you to stream gameplay from your XBOX Series X|S to devices you already own, like mobile devices, PCs, and handheld gaming PCs. Here’s how to enable it: Once you’ve completed those steps above, you can move forward with Remote Play on one of your devices: Whether you’re streaming from the Cloud to save space or picking up right where you left off on your handheld PC, XBOX Cloud Gaming and Remote Play give you more ways to play Grand Theft Auto VI on the devices you already own. sources.name: GamesIndustry.biz
sources.title: Staff at Grand Theft Auto maker Rockstar vote against union recognition deal
sources.text: Workers at Grand Theft Auto maker Rockstar Games have voted against a union recognition deal. 1,544 staff members took part in the vote across the company's locations in Edinburgh, Leeds, Lincoln, Dundee and London, representing a 93.2% turnout. Despite this huge engagement, 75.3% voted against Independent Workers of Great Britain (IWGB) union recognition, while 24.7% voted in favour. Had this vote gone the other way, IWGB Rockstar Game Workers Union would have been the biggest recognised union in the UK games industry, and Rockstar would have been obligated to engage with collective bargaining on pay and working hours. "We are extraordinarily proud of our team, the culture we've built together and the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6," the company's head of publishing, Jennifer Kolbe, said in a statement. "This result reflects our team's strong support for continuing the direct relationships, collaboration and open dialogue that have helped make Rockstar Games so innovative and strong. As we look ahead, we're excited to build on all we've accomplished together," said a company rep. IWGB says that Rockstar staff will keep organising regardless of whether the union is formally recognised. "For anyone at Rockstar who believes in a fairer workplace, a fairer sector and a fairer society – this isn’t a sign to retreat, it’s a sign to double down on what we stand for," the organisation said in its own statement. "Hundreds of our coworkers voted in favour of our union at Rockstar, yet sadly we recognise we have more work to do to build understanding and win the trust of more of our colleagues. We’re ready to put in the effort to make that happen. "Whilst we haven’t emerged with a recognition deal, this ballot has put our union on the radar of every worker, and opened the door for new kinds of conversation to start happening. People entirely unfamiliar with unions were for the first time debating employment conditions, collective bargaining rights, and our contracts. We heard from many more colleagues about what mattered to them, and we hope people will continue to engage so that we can see where these new discussions can lead us. "A recognition agreement would have marked a path towards greater workplace democracy. But it’s one route of many. At Rockstar we have already won, and will continue to win, tangible changes that improve our everyday lives. We’ll keep fighting for a say. For pay transparency, contractual overtime pay, and protections against AI and layoffs. "The power to shape our working lives has always been, and will always be, in our hands." Under UK law, the union may not re-apply for recognition for three years, although staff remain free to join the RGWU. The question of forming a union at Rockstar Games followed allegations that 34 members of staff were let go from the Grand Theft Auto maker in a move that IWGB called union-busting . Rockstar parent company Take-Two has denied this claim, saying that staff were fired for "distributing and discussing confidential information". Rockstar and IWGB are currently embroiled in an employment tribunal regarding these job cuts; closing arguments were issued on November 19 . Judge Lucy Wiseman, who oversaw proceedings, said that there is no timeframe yet for the judgement, but said she would try her best to "get that judgement out as quickly as possible". Grand Theft Auto 6 launched on November 19th and made a record $3.79 billion in revenue in its first 24 hours on sale .

sources.title: Chainsaws 'Would Have Been Too Much' Even for GTA 6, as Rockstar Explains Why Some Extra Violent Weapons Are Missing
sources.text: You can commit an extreme amount of violence in GTA 6 , with a wide variety of weaponry. Guns, baseball bats, even tanks can be your chosen tool of destruction. But that hasn’t stopped some from wondering where some series favourites have disappeared to. Among those are the likes of katanas and chainsaws, which were staples during Grand Theft Auto’s “3D universe” games, including Vice City and San Andreas. The chainsaw, in particular, holds a special connection to Vice City given its clear Scarface inspirations, and memorable scene involving the power tool from the 1983 movie. But despite some being spotted around the latest version of Leonida in GTA 6, neither Jason nor Lucia can wield them as weapons. Why? Well, Rockstar co-studio head Rob Nelson explained the decision in an interview with VGC . “As far as the chainsaw — I think it would have been too much for this game at this resolution and these characters,” Nelson says. "It’s not a resource thing. Even at the most psycho, did Jason and Lucia really need that — what’s that going to look like?” When asked specifically about why chainsaws are lying about the world, but can’t be picked up, Nelson explained that, “you’re always trying to find what is the right sort of line and the right balance; it really just depends — you want to feel like you can interact with as much of the world as possible.” I have to somewhat agree that it just wouldn’t feel like it fit either Jason or Lucia’s characters to be roaming around looking for limbs to chop off with a mechanised serrated blade. Ultimately, their story is one about committing crime to escape to a better, more “normal” life, not one about two psychopaths with a lust for blood going on a rampage. That being said, when whatever the online component of GTA 6 launches, I could see objects like this becoming weapons, allowing for people to roleplay as whatever brand of criminal, psychopath, or tree sculptor they wish. There’s a world of possibilities out there. Just getting started in GTA 6 or wondering what to do next? Check out the Official Grand Theft Auto 6 guide right here on IGN. If you're still getting your bearings, discover GTA's new systems with the Beginner's Guide - 67 Tips and Tricks , or get all the details on the first chapters with the Chapter 1 Guide and Tips , Chapter 2 Guide and Tips , and Chapter 3 Guide and Tips . If you're already driving all around Leonida and want to know everything there is to find and do, see the Leonida interactive map . Simon Cardy is a Senior Editor at IGN who can mainly be found skulking around open world games, indulging in Korean cinema, or despairing at the state of Tottenham Hotspur and the New York Jets. Follow him on Bluesky at @cardy.bsky.social .

stories.summary: Developer Playground Games had to look beyond Lionhead's original run of Fable games when rebooting the classic fantasy series, and it's all thanks to games like The Witcher 3 , which changed what many players expect from their big RPGs and set a new "gold standard." Read more

sources.name: Eurogamer
sources.title: The Fable reboot had to look beyond Lionhead's RPG trilogy because games like The Witcher 3 "became the gold standard"
sources.text: Developer Playground Games had to look beyond Lionhead's original run of Fable games when rebooting the classic fantasy series, and it's all thanks to games like The Witcher 3 , which changed what many players expect from their big RPGs and set a new "gold standard." The upcoming Fable reboot is finally ending its decade-long development journey soon. Playground Games had to set up an entirely new team to work on its fairytale revival, so Fable's production wasn't quite as smooth sailing as the studio's consistently excellent Forza Horizon series, for example. Asked about what's changed during that time, in an interview with GamesIndustry.biz , studio founder and general manager Ralph Fulton named technological advancements as a biggie, but the impact of other games was perhaps even greater. "In 2015, The Witcher 3 redefined what an open-world action RPG looks like and became the gold standard," Fulton said. "And after that bar was raised, the Assassin's Creed franchise changed into this more modern iteration with Origins, Odyssey, and Valhalla, and became like a quasi-RPG." "All of these games continue to reset player expectations," he continued. Millions of players suddenly had certain expectations about what their big-budget, open-world role-playing games should look like. So, Playground couldn't pull inspiration from Fable and Fable alone. "I think looking only to the original Fable trilogy for inspiration would leave us lacking in terms of what the modern audience, the modern marketplace, expects," Fulton added. Still, Playground's Fable is drawing most heavily from Lionhead's Fable. Fulton specifically mentions the game's signature British wit and in-flux morality system as examples. Then there's also the spontaneous life sim elements that "none of our competitors do," according to Fulton. "It's a totally Fable thing, the social simulation and economic simulation. Okay, there are games that have economic simulations, but they're not in [our] RPG category. Fable is unique in that it's almost like a life sim in terms of genre." Raising four separate families and becoming the entire map's benevolent landlord was one of the funnest parts of Fable back in the day, alongside those sometimes silly characters. Seeing next year's Fable lean into those systemic choices, and having Albion's NPCs react to them more believably, could give this one a very long shelf life.

sources.name: Kotaku
sources.title: Here Are Some Video Game Conversation Starters That Aren’t About GTA 6
sources.text: It’s the Thanksgiving holiday weekend. Millions of people will soon be gathering with family, catching everybody up on the goings-on in their lives over the past year. A subset of those people will be gamers, who may be subject to blank stares from aunts and uncles whose conception of the multibillion-dollar industry has not progressed beyond calling every console a “Nintendo” or confused inquiries from relatives who’ve just recently been made aware that video games are a thing by all the breathless coverage of GTA 6 on network television. She has never really taken an interest in what I do, and while that stings a bit, she is at least happy that I am happy in my chosen profession and that’s good enough for me. In one of the exceedingly rare times that she has ever asked me directly about my job, she called me the other day asking if I was “excited” for the pending release of GTA 6. She used stronger language than “excited” but I’m not gonna repeat exactly what she said to me because it’s something no child should ever hear their parent say to them in any context but it involved “cream” and “drawers” so draw your own conclusions. I explained to her that 1) ew and 2) I’m not excited per se, but I am interested to see what happens with this game and how we talk about it. But I also told her that despite the sensational coverage of the game, its development price tag, and its status as the most anticipated game this decade…it’s not for me. I’ve never been into those games and I don’t see GTA 6 changing that stance much. We quickly moved on to other topics. At first, this exchange reopened that unhealed wound of “I wish you took a greater interest in the thing I’ve built a life on.” If she had, she might know that I’m more of a Kingdom Heart s girlie, the game I used to play by ferrying my PS2 from its box under my bed to the 12-inch tube TV in her room when I was 16 years old. But as I think about it now, even though she’s wildly missed the mark on my tastes and preferences, I actually really appreciate that she asked at all. She saw a video game on TV and thought, “Oh hey, my daughter does video games, let me talk to her about that.” That was her attempt at connecting with me, and it’s way more than a lot of other parents do when it comes to engaging with their children’s passion professions, so thanks, mom. You, too, might be a person who has a gamer in your life who you’ll have the chance to catch up with this holiday weekend. And while there’s a very good chance that, unlike me, they’re actually into GTA 6, here’s a quick list of topics to broach just in case they’re not. Ask this question and, depending on the gamer you target with this, you’ll either get an excited offer to play or a thoughtful discussion on the ethics of using generative AI in video game development . Be careful with this one. Whether they have or they haven’t, they’re about to cry . This is a fun one because you’re about to sit with your gamer for hours as they try to hash out exactly how many Final Fantasy games there are. Bring snacks. And finally, the best question you can ask any gamer in your life: Donât miss the latest reviews, news and tips. Sign up for our free newsletter. sources.title: The latest adult game in the Muv-Luv series has some woeful AI translation and players aren't happy about it
sources.text: The store page boasts "over 800,000 copies sold worldwide" but user reviews have sunk to Mostly Negative. The Muv-Luv trilogy is a visual novel phenomenon that's tough to explain. The first game's a schlocky high school romance generally considered a chore to get through before the good stuff, when the protagonist of that story finds himself out of his depth as a mecha pilot fighting aliens in an apocalyptic warzone. It becomes a dense, twisty, and increasingly serious saga that just happens to star a dropkick hero right out of a harem anime. Muv-Luv's popular enough to have a bunch of spin-offs, the latest being a gacha game called Muv-Luv Girls Garden in which you collect girls to pilot mecha in automated battles, and of course said girls are romanceable. This caused a problem, as players discovered when they made it to some of the adult scenes only to find dialogue in which characters repeated at each other, "I can't provide a translation for explicit sexual content." Yeah, Muv-Luv Girls Garden was translated into English with AI. The Steam page does mention this in its AI-generated content disclosure, though hilariously it does so in untranslated Japanese: "1部ローカライズに生成AIを使用しています。" Players are unimpressed, with the Steam user rating dropping to Mostly Negative. As one user review puts it, "What if you want to goon But God says I'm unable to provide a translation for this text because it contains explicit sexual content ." Other user reviews complain about changes to the original artwork, with characters having accessories like teddy bears and hair ribbons taken away, as well as being given larger breasts or made to look taller. It's tougher to emphasize with players who are mad that characters in an adult game have been changed to look less like 12-year-olds, especially given the pressure put on Valve by payment processors to remove certain kinds of games from Steam. stories.summary: Catch Port Gellhorn's creepy serial killer and end the 20-year mystery.

sources.name: PC Gamer
sources.title: All Missing Persons locations in GTA 6
sources.text: Catch Port Gellhorn's creepy serial killer and end the 20-year mystery. The GTA 6 Missing Persons case is available as early as Chapter 1, but you'll need access to both Lucia and Jason to wrap up the side quest in Chapter 2. Your stint as a fledgling detective begins in an abandoned warehouse near Mo's shop in Gellhorn, though there are two ways to flag the objective on your map and start the hunt for Gellhorn's serial killer. If you begin in Chapter 1 when you can only play as Jason, head straight to the abandoned warehouse to begin. This is how I began the quest the first time, after following a pack of coyotes through a small opening on the side of the abandoned warehouse. This route gives you an extra text conversation where Jason sends Lucia creepy photos from the warehouse. Begin in Chapter 2 by heading to the Starlet Motel lobby in Gellhorn and inspecting the missing persons posters. Afterward, head to the abandoned warehouse as a couple or go alone, and squeeze through the crawl space. After crawling inside the warehouse, walk to the far end and turn right to enter the glowing red room. Go a little farther to find the, uh, "trophies," and inspect all three lockers, along with the missing persons posters on the wall. This is where you begin your hunt for Gellhorn's three missing tourists. I've got all three locations highlighted below, but if you want to solve it yourself, now is the time to turn back. The first missing person in northwest Gellhorn is in an abandoned trailer—the water tower's shadow is your giveaway. Run along the fence and enter the blue building from the back. There's an awfully suspicious hole in the floor, so pull the remaining floorboards back to discover what's left of Patrick Murray. Call the Kelly County Tip Line after you find Patrick's remains and leave a message. No one will answer the phone, for now. Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team. The second missing person is in the junkyard, inside the trunk of an old pink DeVanity. The junkyard is right beside Pay 'n' Spray off Gellhorn Ave, across the street from the drive-in theatre. You'll spot Susanne Keeble's pink car with the PRTYGRL license plate while facing the drive-in. After finding a second body, call the tip line again to finally speak to an investigator. They're thrilled to hear there's renewed interest in the case, and ask that you keep in contact should you make any further discoveries. The third missing person is in a U-shaped inlet off the Borrachero Sound. You can find the smaller body of water by traveling southeast from the Wild Hog Point hangar. The view of Wild Hog Point from the tree in the creepy photo is your giveaway, so start looking for a submerged car when you find the right perspective. After finding a third body, the investigator from the tip line asks to meet in the abandoned warehouse. And no, it's not just you, it's a pretty shady proposition. When you're ready for the meeting, consider whether you want to go with your partner or go alone. Both seem to give me the same boost to Jason and Lucia's relationship status, elevating it to Hot Together (4/4) status for the first time in Chapter 2. It had dropped all the way down to Partners in Crime (2/4) just before this, so the Missing Persons quest was a much-appreciated bump. You can also get the serial killer's glasses from his body if you choose to continue as a couple. They're beyond creepy, so I wouldn't blame you if you left them there, but aside from that, there's no cash reward. You will have to do it, though, if you're going for a 100% GTA 6 run. As either Jason or Lucia, return to the abandoned warehouse trophy room and meet Alvan West—the man you spoke to on the Kelly County Tips Line. He's got a 'surprise' waiting for you in the fourth locker, and a fight ensues after checking it out. Going alone means there's no one there to save the passed out Jason or Lucia, and the serial killer takes them to a cave in Lummox County. The attack automatically triggers a character swap, leaving you to investigate your partner's whereabouts after receiving suspicious texts. Enter the abandoned warehouse trophy room just like before while your partner waits outside. When they sense something is off, they'll run inside to save you just as you pass out. After Alvan is dead, inspect his body—you can take his glasses as a souvenir. That's freak behavior, but I'm not judging. We gotta get that 100% cosmetic collection somehow. Outside of those staples, she's often got a few survival-crafting games on rotation and loves a good scare in co-op horror games. sources.text: How to complete the President’s Bunker mission in GTA 6 Wondering how to open the President’s Bunker in GTA 6? The President’s Bunker hidden mission in GTA 6 is one of the most complex, but with this guide, you’ll be able to complete it and get the secret tank as a reward. This GTA 6 President’s Bunker walkthrough explains how to start the mission, find both bunkers, discover every code and collect the exclusive rewards, including a unique pistol, an assault rifle and a military tank. For even more GTA 6 guides, check out our GTA 6 walkthrough hub. Guides: If you're playing Grand Theft Auto 6, make sure to checkÂ out ourÂ complete walkthrough hub , featuringÂ beginner tips , navigation experience explained , GTA 6 cheats , and more. The GTA 6 President’s Bunker mission starts in Downtown Vice City by speaking to a random man near a statue that comemorates the war. Start by travelling to Downtown, specifically the Friends of Freedom memorial on Catalan Boulevard. Check the image above for the speficic location. The memorial is dedicated to President Joe Russo and is located in the eastern part of Downtown.Look for an elderly man sitting near the memorial wall. This is Jose Bermudez, the character who introduces players to the hidden bunker storyline. Approach him and start a conversation. When the dialogue options appear, select: Jose will begin explaining his version of the Presidential assassination and reveal that he has evidence connected to the incident. This is the start of a questline that leads you to the President’s Bunker.Â He will also direct you towards his apartment in Little Cuba. He notes that you can find this apartment by looking for a large number of Cuban flags outside the door. Your next destination is Little Cuba, specifically NW 4th Avenue. Look for a salmon-coloured building decorated with Cuban flags, located near a vehicle modification shop. You can see an image of the apartment building below.Â Enter the building and head upstairs to find Jose’s apartment. Inside the apartment, there are several important clues that you should investigate: Make sure you listen to the complete recording rather than leaving halfway through. The information provided here becomes important when accessing the first bunker if you’re completing the quest organically. I suppose if you’re reading this then you don’t need to do this at all. Come to think of it, I don’t even know if you need to do this part of the quest before you head to Sharktooth Island. Once you’ve finished investigating Jose’s apartment, it’s time to travel to the first bunker. The facility is located on Sharktooth Island, a small island north of Waning Sands. Because the location is surrounded by water, taking a boat is recommended. You can also swim across, although travelling by boat is considerably more convenient. If you get stuck out there, there’s a boat that spawns on the opposite shore of the island from the bunker itself. On the north shore of Sharktooth Island, you’ll find the entrance to the bunker. Interact with the keypad and enter the following code: After entering the bunker, you’ll discover that the facility has no electricity. Follow the underground passage and look for the power switch. Turn right inside the tunnel to locate the electrical control panel. Interact with it to restore power. Once the electricity is working, return through the passage and take the opposite route into the main bunker. You’ll now be able to investigate the presidential facility. Inside the bunker, look around for documents, recordings and other evidence. On one desk there’s a picture of President Russo meeting with an alien on Mount Chilliad. Mount Chilliad was the site of much speculation in te GTA 5 era due to clues about an apart alien mystery, and the fact that a UFO would appear over the mountain when players 100%’d the game. Continue looking around the room until you reach the presidential desk. Interact with the desk and investigate its contents. This will help activate the next part of the puzzle. Jason or Lucia will sit back and begin to make jokes about them being President. It doesn’t matter which of the two you play as. The presidential safe contains one of the most valuable rewards in the entire bunker mission: Russo’s 1922 Pistol. However, opening it requires solving a small puzzle. Here it is in beat-by-beat steps. Enter the combination into the safe to unlock it. Inside, you’ll find Russo’s 1922 Pistol and a mysterious photograph which leads to the second part of the quest. Make sure you collect the pistol and inspect the photograph before leaving. On the back of the picture you’ll find the word: OBSESS. This is the code to enter the second bunker. It is an underground IAA black site located in the forests of North Mariana County, close to the Big Pine area. Travel towards the forested area near Big Pine. Look for a hidden underground hatch rather than the large bunker door. You can see it pictured below.Â The keypad to enter the bunker is attached to a nearby tree, making it relatively easy to miss if you’re simply searching for a conventional entrance. The code comes from converting the word OBSESS into its corresponding seven-segment display numbers. Once you’ve entered the correct combination, the hatch will open. Climb down the ladder to enter the underground IAA facility. Like the first bunker, the second bunker is extremely dark, so having a flashlight available is recommended. Once you’re in the facility, stick to the left wall and follow it to a far off room. In here you’ll find another electricity panel like the one from the first bunker.Â Interact with it to restore electricity. Once the power is restored, you should be able to investigate the rest of the facility. Continue exploring the facility and follow the sounds of the recording devices. stories.title: Ubisoft argued calling Skull and Bones a AAAA game wasn't "misleading," but "classic puffery"
stories.summary: Statements about Skull and Bones were previously argued to have "enticed consumers to enter into consumer transactions to their detriment"

sources.name: GamesRadar
sources.title: Ubisoft argued calling Skull and Bones a AAAA game wasn't "misleading," but "classic puffery"
sources.text: Statements about Skull and Bones were previously argued to have "enticed consumers to enter into consumer transactions to their detriment" Remember when Ubisoft boss Yves Guillemot said the company was making the world's first AAAA video game with its mediocre pirate RPG Skull and Bones? Well, that terminology landed Ubisoft in a bit of hot water – which it may have gotten itself out of for now, but potentially not forever. As reported by Game File , a lawsuit was filed against Ubisoft in 2025 by a gamer (and lawyer) who alleged that the company had violated Kansas' consumer protection act with its marketing of Skull and Bones, partly pointing to Guillemot calling it a AAAA game when trying to justify its $70 price tag in an earnings call. In the same call, Guillemot had called it "a very big game" that was "vast and complete," and said it would "deliver in the long run." Obviously, when it came down to it, more than a few players disagreed with this sentiment, with a Metacritic score of 59 and a user score of 3.3 essentially dubbing it mid at best. Certainly not what anyone was hoping for after over 10 years of development. Needless to say, the game-loving lawyer wasn't impressed, and in the initial lawsuit, it was alleged: "The statements by the CEO were misleading and enticed consumers to enter into consumer transactions to their detriment." Ubisoft, however, didn't agree that Guillemot had been misleading, calling his comments "subjective statements" and "classic puffery" – defined in this context as exaggerated statements not intended to be taken literally as fact. As such, the company's lawyers argued: "Plaintiff has not identified a single objective statement about the game's quality that is demonstrably untrue, let alone one that he saw or relied on in purchasing the game as is required under the KCPA [Kansas Consumer Protection Act]." However, the lawsuit argued that because Guillemot's comments were made during an earnings call, they were directed at investors rather than customers, and therefore the CEO "knew or should have known his statements would be relied upon as credible and truthful." The issue went "beyond mere puffery," it was argued. Game File points out, though, just how 'AAAA' Skull and Bones is wasn't actually the focus of the argument. Rather, the main point was an alleged digital ownership issue, with claims that fans had been misled into thinking they'd own the game rather than simply its license – a license that, in theory, he could lose access to. However, a judge sided with Ubisoft back in August. Even so, the lawyer suggested that he'll re-file it in California – Ubisoft had previously argued it required the case to be transferred there – so it might not be over for good yet. Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more Whether that AAAA game comment comes back to bite Ubisoft again is another matter, though. Regardless of whether the company is legally in the clear for using it, one CD Projekt Red exec previously appeared to poke fun at it , and more generally it doesn't seem likely that folks are going to let Ubisoft forget about it. Ubisoft's ridiculous "AAAA" term still refuses to die as producer reportedly says Assassin's Creed Shadows and Mirage come under that umbrella, too. I'm GamesRadar+'s Deputy News Editor, working alongside the rest of the news team to deliver cool gaming stories that we love. After spending more hours than I can count filling The University of Sheffield's student newspaper with Pokemon and indie game content, and picking up a degree in Journalism Studies, I started my career at GAMINGbible where I worked as a journalist for over a year and a half. I then became TechRadar Gaming's news writer, where I sourced stories and wrote about all sorts of intriguing topics. In my spare time, you're sure to find me on my Nintendo Switch or PS5 playing through story-driven RPGs like Xenoblade Chronicles and Persona 5 Royal, nuzlocking old Pokemon games, or going for a Victory Royale in Fortnite. sources.title: Ubisoft defends calling Skull & Bones a ‘quadruple-A’ game in lawsuit
sources.text: Ubisoft argues that the “quadruple-A” comments were just Yves Guillemot’s opinion Ubisoft is fighting a lawsuit over how it promoted and sold Skull & Bones to customers. As reported by Game File , part of the lawsuit concerns how Ubisoft CEO Yves Guillemot described Skull & Bones as Ubisoft’s first “quadruple-A game” to justify its higher price point. Now, Ubisoft argues that this statement from Guillemot was “classic puffery” – a legal term that defends making “subjective and exaggerated statements” about an item that is being sold. The Plaintiff – Jacob Himberger – is a lawyer who bought and played Skull & Bones . He argues that calling the game quadruple-A was “misleading” to consumers, something Ubisoft rejects. “It appears Plaintiff intends to argue that subjective statements from Mr. Guillemot about the forthcoming release were misleading,” say Ubisoft’s lawyers. “However, such statements â including that a video game is ‘really big’, ‘vast and complete’, or ‘triple â¦ quadruple-A’ – are classic puffery and not actionable under the [Kansas Consumer Protection and Accountability Act]. “Plaintiff has not identified a single objective statement about the gameâs quality that is demonstrably untrue, let alone one that he saw or relied on in purchasing the game as is required under the KCPA.” In other words, Ubisoft wants claims that a game is quadruple-A as opposed to triple-A to be protected, arguing that this cannot be disproven, unlike a claim about how the game performs or what features it contains. At the time, Guillemot’s comments about Skull & Bones were widely mocked in the gaming community. The game would go on to launch in February 2024 to mixed reviews, following several lengthy delays. Himberger’s lawsuit against Ubisoft also concerns game ownership. He argues that he was led to believe he would own Skull & Bones, not just a licence for it. So far, attempts to legislate on this in favour of consumers have proven unsuccessful , particularly when it comes to digital game purchases.
